quotes.quote: Found only in the Mekong River basin in Cambodia, around Stung Treng.

sections.html:
Betta stiktos is the rarest member of the Betta splendens complex. IUCN Red List: Data Deficient (not enough information, but most likely highly endangered in the wild). The specimens in trade are captive bred from wild-caught stock.

It looks similar to Betta smaragdina but has a smaller, stouter body, shorter fins and a spotted dorsal fin. The species was once thought to be extinct, but it has reappeared in the hobby through a handful of breeders.
Found only in the Mekong River basin in Cambodia, around Stung Treng.
Lives in swampy streams and ponds with dense vegetation and low oxygen, in still, slightly acidic water (pH 5 to 7.5) at 22 to 27°C. It uses its labyrinth organ to breathe air.

Body: compact and slender with a stout head. Smaller than most splendens-complex relatives, reaching about 2.8 cm standard length; maximum size given as 5 cm. Tail: exclusively roundtail, with short caudal and anal fins, up to 9 rows of black transverse bars on the caudal fin and 5 rows of round black spots on the dorsal fin. The snake-scale pattern is lighter on the body and much more prominent on the face and gill plates.

• Temperature: 24 to 29°C (coloration is much better above 26°C)
  • pH: 5.0 to 7.0
  • TDS: 60 to 200; kept in soft, low-TDS water, but tolerates a wider range
Carnivorous. Accepts live blackworms, frozen bloodworms and pellets.
Males are very aggressive and should be kept alone or with non-male betta tankmates. Multiple females can be kept together in a planted community tank if there is enough space.

Males are brown to black with iridescent green-blue and possible red patches on the fins. Females are browner with faint green. The operculum is black with a prominent, widespread snake-scale pattern of iridescent green-blue, strongest in males.

Bubblenester. The male builds a bubble nest under a floating leaf or plants and places the eggs in it after spawning. Remove the female once spawning is done. Eggs hatch in 24 to 48 hours, and the fry are free-swimming about 3 days later. Start them on infusoria, then move to baby brine shrimp. Keep the surface calm so the nest stays intact.
